sources.entry: miniserve - CLI tool to serve files and dirs over HTTP. MIT Rust

summary.one_liner: miniserve is a small, self-contained Rust CLI tool that serves files and directories over HTTP from the command line with a single command.
summary.what_it_does: Serves a single file or a directory from the command line, with a directory listing or a custom index file. Optional features include username/password auth (plain, SHA-256/SHA-512 hashed, or from a file), TLS with custom certificate and key, and custom response headers. Users can enable file uploading, directory creation, file and directory deletion, and a pastebin, each behind its own flag. Folders can be downloaded as tar, tar.gz, or zip archives when enabled. It also offers search/filter by name, SPA and pretty-URL modes, read-only WebDAV (PROPFIND), QR code display, and multiple color themes.
use_cases: quickly share files over HTTP from a terminal
serve a directory to a colleague on the local network
receive file or photo uploads from a phone or browser
host a single-page application build locally
run a simple HTTPS file server with a custom certificate
notable: Single binary with no extra runtime dependencies, available for Linux, macOS, Windows, and Termux
Random 6-hex-digit URL route option for obscuring a share
Separate --file-external-url option to pair an authenticated browsing instance with a non-indexed download instance
Hardened systemd unit template for running one instance per served path
Built-in shell completions and man page generation
caveats: Zip archive generation happens in memory, so large directories can cause out-of-memory errors (per the README)
TLS is listed as supported only on supported architectures
WebDAV support is read-only (PROPFIND requests only)
